items.slide_topic: Continual Learning and Test Time Training
items.headline: End-to-End Test-Time Training for Long Context
items.dek: Figure 1: Scaling with context length, in terms of test loss (left) and latency (right).
items.author: Arnuv Tandon, Karan Dalal, Xinhao Li, Daniel Koceja, Marcel Rød, Sam Buchanan, Xiaolong Wang, Jure Leskovec, Sanmi Koyejo, Tatsunori Hashimoto, Carlos Guestrin, Jed McCaleb, Yejin Choi, Yu Sun
items.caption: TTT-E2E Fig. 1: left = loss delta vs full attention (TTT-E2E stays ~-0.012 to -0.014 from 8K to 128K while other efficient models degrade); right = prefill latency per 1K tokens (flat for TTT-E2E, full attention climbs to ~2.7x at 128K on an H100). Rendered from the paper's own SVGs (flagship.svg, timing.svg).
items.notes: Panels also saved separately: ttt_e2e_fig1_left_loss.png, ttt_e2e_fig1_right_latency.png (1800x1480 each). Combined is 3700x1480, white background.

items.slide_topic: Continual Learning and Test Time Training
items.headline: End-to-End Test-Time Training for Long Context (arXiv:2512.23675)
items.dek: "We formulate long-context language modeling as a problem in continual learning rather than architecture design... our model continues learning at test time via next-token prediction on the given context, compressing the context it reads into its weights." ... "similar to RNNs, TTT-E2E has constant inference latency regardless of context length, making it 2.7 times faster than full attention for 128K context."
items.caption: Abstract quotes (v2 revised 2025-12-31). Code: https://github.com/test-time-training/e2e
items.notes: Also: '3B models trained with 164B tokens ... scales with context length in the same way as Transformer with full attention, while others, such as Mamba 2 and Gated DeltaNet, do not.'

items.slide_topic: Continual Learning and Test Time Training
items.headline: TTT-E2E limitations (Table 2 / Figure 8 captions)
items.dek: Table 2: "Transformer with full attention dramatically outperforms the other methods, including ours, especially in long context" (S-NIAH needle-in-a-haystack). Figure 8: "training latency is still a significant limitation of our current implementation."
items.caption: Honesty caveat for speaker notes: weights-as-memory compresses context (lossy recall); the paper evaluates up to 128K, so 'effectively infinite context' is an extrapolation of the constant-latency property, not a tested claim.

items.slide_topic: Continual Learning and Test Time Training
items.headline: Self-Guided Test-Time Training for Long-Context LLMs (arXiv:2607.09415)
items.dek: "A promising way to improve long-context utilization is test-time training (TTT), which treats the test context as a training example for instance-specific parameter adaptation." ... S-TTT "improves accuracy for both Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, achieving up to a 15% relative improvement."
items.author: Xinyu Zhu, Zhe Xu, Xiaohan Wei, Yunchen Pu, Fei Tian, Chonglin Sun, Kaushik Rangadurai, Hua Zhi, Frank Shyu, Sandeep Pandey, Luke Simon, Yu Meng, Xi Liu
items.caption: Follow-on 2026 TTT work (surfaced in the other session's web search; abstract verified here).

items.headline: An Alien Mind
items.dek: "This tool continues to be critical as we study the Astra class of models. However, unfortunately our evaluations indicate our ability to rely on CoT monitoring is progressively diminishing." ... "With improved pretraining performance, we also see the models become much smarter even without using verbalized reasoning at all." ... "Based on internal results, I have a strong expectation that this speed of progress could be sustained into recursive self-improvement." ... "Currently I believe that no lab has solved alignment and monitoring to a sufficient degree to continue responsibly scaling at maximum speed for much longer."

items.headline: OpenAI's new reasoning technique alarms AI safety experts
items.dek: OpenAI's new Astra model will use "recurrent depth," a technique that allows it to operate outside sequential thinking, making the model's chain of thought harder to monitor.
items.author: Russell Brandom
items.caption: Quotes: Buck Shlegeris: "...they'll have the option to massively increase the recurrence and totally destroys CoT monitorability." Ryan Greenblatt: "a natural progression from here would involve scaling up the opaque reasoning to the point where the model reasons entirely or almost entirely in latent space."
items.notes: Other session captured h12_techcrunch_opaque_recurrence.png (not available here).

items.headline: Research acceleration: The view inside OpenAI
items.dek: "According to our measurements, we have now reached the goal, announced last fall, of having an automated research intern by September of this year." ... "We are making strong progress toward creating an automated AI researcher by March of 2028." ... "as of mid-August, in total, the research organization uses 3.1 agent-workdays of effort for every workday of human labor."
items.caption: Also: median researcher >$600/day of agent inference, 90th percentile >$7,000/day; RL training paused ~2 weeks after the Hugging Face incident (July 20); Astra-class GPU allocation fell a further 59.2% after Aug 7 cyber-capability finding.
items.notes: Other session saved its charts (f02 agent-workdays, f03 lines changed, f04 task success, f05 RL compute pause, f06 experiment velocity) on its cluster.

items.headline: When AI builds itself

By April 2026, Claude Mythos Preview was achieving ~52x"; "On the most open-ended tasks, Claude's success rate reached 76% in May 2026"

facts.claim: TTT-E2E treats long context as continual learning: the model keeps training on its context at test time, compressing it into its weights.
Constant inference latency regardless of context length: 2.7x faster than full attention at 128K tokens (H100), while matching full attention's scaling with context (3B params, 164B tokens).
OpenAI's chief scientist: 'our ability to rely on CoT monitoring is progressively diminishing.'
Astra uses 'recurrent depth' / opaque recurrence, making its chain of thought harder to monitor.
OpenAI says it reached an 'automated research intern' by Sept 2026 and targets an automated AI researcher by March 2028; its research org runs 3.1 agent-workdays per human workday.
Anthropic: more than 80% of merged code is authored by Claude; engineers merge 8x as much code per day as in 2024.
